subject: Horizon Health — model fit recommendations & quant trade plan
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@hhcorp.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: model fit + quantization trade plan (next steps)

Hi Alice — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we can align engineering and procurement.

Recap (short):
- Goal: accurate, concise patient summary extraction and downstream clinical note generation with 95%+ acceptability on the human eval set.
- Current constraints: 2s tail-latency target at p95, cost sensitivity for high-volume nightly batches, and a requirement to avoid hallucination of PHI.

Recommended model candidates for evaluation (initial shortlist):
- rwd-7b-awq (Redwood-curated AWQ profile) — best memory footprint, designed for high throughput.
- meta-13b-gptq — strong fidelity in our internal summarization tests, larger footprint.
- llama-2-13b-fp8 (FP8 on A100) — promising for throughput with near-float32 quality in some downstream tasks (needs careful ops).

Artifacts attached: horizon_bench_20270401.csv (microbenchmarks on your sample corpus), prompt_set_health_summaries_v1.txt (the prompt sets we ran), and a 1-page quant_tradeoff_onepager.pdf with a quick trade summary. Also shared a read-only Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c_horizon-evals

Key quality note: our initial AWQ runs show ~2–3% BLEU/ROUGE degradation on the clinical summary subset versus GPTQ, but latency/cost improves 30–45%. We view this as a trade candidate rather than a disqualifier — the important thing is to validate on your acceptance prompts and clinician review set.

Proposed next steps (please confirm which you want us to start):
1) Run an A/B evaluation across the three profiles using your clinician prompt set (we can use the attached prompt_set as a starting point). Budget: ~2k sample tokens to start.
2) Surface per-prompt failure cases and hallucination triggers — we’ll tag and share canonical repro examples.
3) If AWQ shows unacceptable quality regressions on your red prompts, fallback plan: evaluate GPTQ at medium quant (4-bit variant) and FP8 on A100s for the production path.
4) Schedule a technical working session next week to lock performance SLOs and region (we can run in us-west-2 or us-east-1).

Proposed time for the working session: Tue 2027-04-06 10:00am PT — does that work?

Thanks — I’ll start prepping the eval harness once you confirm.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com

Thanks Kimberly — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Quality concern: our clinical reviewers are particularly sensitive to even small hallucination increases when extracting medication regimens. If AWQ causes a consistent ~3% drop in metrics, that might be a blocker unless we can bias prompts or post-process reliably. Can you point to the failure modes you saw in the attached prompt set?

2) Hardware preference: our infra team prefers to avoid large A100 commitments upfront. If FP8 requires A100-only, we’ll need a deeper cost analysis.

3) Timeline: we can commit to a 2-week eval window starting Mon 2027-04-12 if Redwood can deliver the harness and the per-prompt tagging workflow by then.

Action items for Redwood: please send an explicit plan for the A/B eval, including exact metrics we’ll measure and how we’ll capture clinician labels. Also include an estimate for incremental infra cost per 1M inference tokens for each profile (AWQ/GPTQ/FP8).

We’ll confirm the working session after we see the eval plan.

- Alice
Director of AI, Horizon Health

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Cc: alice.monroe@hhcorp.com, devops@hhcorp.com
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model fit + quantization trade plan (next steps)

Alice / Kim / Ben — quick engineering note on the AWQ / GPTQ / FP8 tradeoffs and a proposed eval matrix. High level:

AWQ (our rwd-7b-awq profile) - Pros: smallest memory footprint, best throughput when using continuous batching + KV cache reuse. In practice we saw 35–45% cost drop on nightly batches in the attached microbench. - Cons: slight degradation on edge-case factuality for very long context prompts; sensitivity increases on token-level n-gram overlap metrics.

GPTQ (meta-13b-gptq) - Pros: fidelity closely matches fp16 in many summarization tests; fewer hallucination triggers in model completions. - Cons: larger model file size and memory requirements; throughput lower unless sharded across more GPUs.

FP8 (llama-2-13b-fp8 on A100) - Pros: throughput similar to AWQ with better numeric fidelity in some tasks; good p95 latency if using dedicated A100 pool. - Cons: deployment maturity is still lower across cloud instance types; not available on cheaper T4/GPU classes.

Proposed A/B eval matrix (we can run in your us-west-2 account with temporary infra):
- Samples: 2k clinical prompts (you provide or we use the shared prompt_set)
- Profiles: rwd-7b-awq vs meta-13b-gptq vs llama-2-13b-fp8
- Metrics: clinician acceptability (binary), hallucination count (per-output annotated), ROUGE-L, token-level perplexity, latency p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens
- Deliverables: per-prompt failure tags, 30 canonical repro cases, aggregated metrics dashboard (CSV + short playbook).

I’ve attached a lightweight runbook and a short csv with the microbench we ran on your sample set (horizon_bench_20270401.csv). If we can get permission for a small test account or provide keys, we’ll spin up a dedicated test harness and run the three profiles in parallel.

Two implementation notes:
1) For hallucination-sensitive prompts we recommend adding a constrained generation wrapper (entity filters + fallback to extraction model) — we can include that in the eval as a toggled variable.
2) If FP8 becomes the chosen path, we suggest a hybrid rollout: use FP8 for high-throughput nightly batches and GPTQ for on-demand low-latency clinician-facing queries.

I’ll draft the cost estimate after we agree on the infra footprint (I can reuse our internal cost model to produce per-1M token numbers).

-Nikhil
Senior Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
